      copilotGain copilotCost delegationCost : ℝ)
    (agentCompetence : ℝ → ℝ) (verificationCost : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (residualVariance : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (hprecision : 0 < precision) : Prop := soloThreshold skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost =
      activationCost - skill * mean + riskAversion * skill ^ 2 / (2 * precision) ∧
    copilotThreshold skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost copilotGain copilotCost =
      soloThreshold skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost -
        (copilotGain * skill - copilotCost) ∧
    generationOneThreshold
        (soloThreshold skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost)
        copilotGain skill copilotCost =
      min (soloThreshold skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost)
        (copilotThreshold skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost
          copilotGain copilotCost) ∧
    delegationThreshold skill mean ability capability delegationShare riskAversion precision
        activationCost delegationCost agentCompetence verificationCost residualVariance =
      activationCost - (1 - delegationShare) * skill * mean -
        delegationShare * ability * agentCompetence capability +
        verificationCost ability skill + delegationCost +
        riskAversion / 2 *
          (((1 - delegationShare) ^ 2 * skill ^ 2) / precision +
            residualVariance ability skill capability) ∧
    generationTwoThreshold
        (generationOneThreshold
          (soloThreshold skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost)
          copilotGain skill copilotCost)
        (delegationThreshold skill mean ability capability delegationShare riskAversion
          precision activationCost delegationCost agentCompetence verificationCost
          residualVariance) =
      min
        (generationOneThreshold
          (soloThreshold skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost)
          copilotGain skill copilotCost)
        (delegationThreshold skill mean ability capability delegationShare riskAversion
          precision activationCost delegationCost agentCompetence verificationCost
          residualVariance) ∧
    (copilotGain * skill - copilotCost ≤ 0 →
      generationOneThreshold
          (soloThreshold skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost)
          copilotGain skill copilotCost =
        soloThreshold skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost) ∧
    soloThreshold skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost -
        delegationThreshold skill mean ability capability delegationShare riskAversion
          precision activationCost delegationCost agentCompetence verificationCost
          residualVariance =
      delegationShare * (ability * agentCompetence capability - skill * mean) -
        verificationCost ability skill - delegationCost +
        riskAversion / 2 *
          (((2 * delegationShare - delegationShare ^ 2) * skill ^ 2) / precision -
            residualVariance ability skill capability)

def generation_menus_and_activitySpec : Prop := ∀ {Language : Type*} (languages : Finset Language)
      (solo copilot delegation : Language → ℝ),
    (∀ language,
      generationOneValue (solo language) (copilot language) =
        max (solo language) (copilot language)) ∧
    (∀ language,
      generationTwoValue (solo language) (copilot language) (delegation language) =
        max (max (solo language) (copilot language)) (delegation language)) ∧
    (∀ language,
      activityIndicator (generationOneValue (solo language) (copilot language)) =
        if 0 ≤ max (solo language) (copilot language) then 1 else 0) ∧
    activeLanguageCount languages (fun language =>
        generationOneValue (solo language) (copilot language)) =
      ∑ language ∈ languages,
        if 0 ≤ max (solo language) (copilot language) then 1 else 0

        "semantic_claim": "The source model assigns skill, general ability, opportunity, activation cost, CARA risk aversion, and Normal productivity beliefs, then defines the solo, conversational-assistant, and delegation certainty-equivalent surpluses by Equations (1)-(3).",
        "source_claim_atom_semantic_sha256": "8dcdf36366b8ec6c7e3184303ac0c9eb9806b83ddab20c24f2c654edfe630e2c",
        "source_locator": "audit/source_archive_surface.tex:179-222",
        "source_quote": "There are developers $i$, programming languages $k\\in\\{1,\\ldots,K\\}$, and\nmonths $t$. Developer $i$ has a familiar-language set $\\mathcal{K}_i$ and\nan unfamiliar set $\\mathcal{U}_i$ with $U_i\\equiv|\\mathcal{U}_i|$; a\nspecialist is a developer with small $|\\mathcal{K}_i|$ and therefore many\nunfamiliar candidates. Empirically, ``unfamiliar'' means not observed in\nthe developer's prior public GitHub contributions; it need not imply\nthat the developer has no private experience with the language. For each developer--language pair, $s_{ik,t}\\in[0,1]$\nis language-specific execution skill, and the developer holds Normal\nbeliefs $\\theta_{ik}\\sim\\N(\\mu_{ik,t},1/\\pi_{ik,t})$ about her latent\nproductivity match, with low skill and low precision in unfamiliar\nlanguages. General ability $a_i\\ge0$ --- the capacity to specify,\ndecompose, and verify a task --- is language-invariant. Each language-month\ncarries an opportunity value $\\omega_{ik,t}$ and an activation cost\n$b_{ik,t}$. The developer has CARA utility with coefficient $\\rho$, so a\npayoff with mean $m$ and variance $\\sigma^2$ has certainty equivalent\n$m-\\rho\\sigma^2/2$ (Appendix \\ref{app:proofs}).\n\nSuppressing $(i,k,t)$ subscripts, the three modes deliver net\ncertainty-equivalent surpluses\n\\begin{align}\nV^S &= \\omega+s\\mu-\\frac{\\rho s^2}{2\\pi}-b,\n\\label{eq:solo-surplus}\\\\\nV^C &= V^S+\\gamma s-r_C,\n\\label{eq:copilot-surplus}\\\\\nV^D &= \\omega+(1-\\lambda)s\\mu+\\lambda a z(A)\n-\\kappa(a,s)-r_D-b\n-\\frac{\\rho}{2}\n\\left[\n\\frac{(1-\\lambda)^2s^2}{\\pi}\n+\\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)\n\\right].\n\\label{eq:delegate-surplus}\n\\end{align}\nSolo production exposes the developer to uncertainty about her own match.\nGeneration-1 augmentation yields a deterministic gain $\\gamma s$\nproportional to existing skill, net of interaction cost $r_C$: the\ndeveloper benefits most when she can read, adapt, and verify the\nsuggestion herself. Generation-2 delegation hands a share\n$\\lambda\\in(0,1]$ of execution to an agent with competence $z(A)$,\nincreasing in capability $A$ and scaled by the developer's general\nability; it carries verification cost $\\kappa(a,s)$, compute cost $r_D$,\nand residual error variance $\\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)$, while shrinking the\nvariance attached to the human match from $s^2/\\pi$ to\n$(1-\\lambda)^2 s^2/\\pi$.",
        "source_quote_sha256": "2b0cdf7f4b8b9b6d5d4be5fd6f4ae255e73733be6f9fd3f219a3db51edd9c0fb"
      }

        "semantic_claim": "Equations (4)-(8) define the solo, conversational, Generation-1, delegation, and Generation-2 activation thresholds and the unfamiliar-language delegation advantage B, including the foothold consequence T1 = TS.",
        "source_claim_atom_semantic_sha256": "b69fdf4191b76e6f6fa191021536180a6cee9dc77b6f0093fbfb212da7f0f7ca",
        "source_locator": "audit/source_archive_surface.tex:251-311",
        "source_quote": "Because each surplus is affine in the opportunity shock $\\omega$, each\nmode has an activation threshold. Setting $V^S\\ge0$ in Equation\n\\eqref{eq:solo-surplus}, solo production is viable when\n\\begin{equation}\n\\omega\\ge\nT^S\\equiv b-s\\mu+\\frac{\\rho s^2}{2\\pi},\n\\label{eq:solo-threshold}\n\\end{equation}\nand since $V^C=V^S+\\gamma s-r_C$, augmentation is viable when\n$\\omega\\ge T^C=T^S-(\\gamma s-r_C)$. The developer takes whichever\npre-agent mode clears first, so the effective Generation-1 threshold is\n\\begin{equation}\nT^1=\\min\\{T^S,T^C\\}\n=T^S-\\max\\{0,\\gamma s-r_C\\},\n\\label{eq:gen1-threshold}\n\\end{equation}\nand for an unfamiliar language Assumption \\ref{ass:foothold} implies\n$\\gamma s-r_C\\le0$, hence $T^1=T^S$: augmentation does not move the\nentry margin. Setting $V^D\\ge0$ in Equation \\eqref{eq:delegate-surplus},\ndelegation is viable when\n\\begin{align}\n\\omega\\ge T^D\n\\equiv{}&\nb-(1-\\lambda)s\\mu-\\lambda a z(A)\n+\\kappa(a,s)+r_D\n\\nonumber\\\\\n&\\quad\n+\\frac{\\rho}{2}\n\\left[\n\\frac{(1-\\lambda)^2s^2}{\\pi}\n+\\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)\n\\right],\n\\label{eq:delegate-threshold}\n\\end{align}\nso the post-agent threshold is $T^2=\\min\\{T^1,T^D\\}\\le T^1$.\n\nFor an unfamiliar language, the economics reduce to the \\emph{agentic\nthreshold reduction} $B\\equiv T^1-T^D=T^S-T^D$. Differencing Equations\n\\eqref{eq:solo-threshold} and \\eqref{eq:delegate-threshold} (algebra in\nAppendix \\ref{app:proofs}) gives\n\\begin{equation}\nB\n=\n\\lambda\\bigl[a z(A)-s\\mu\\bigr]\n-\\kappa(a,s)-r_D\n+\\frac{\\rho}{2}\n\\left[\n\\frac{(2\\lambda-\\lambda^2)s^2}{\\pi}\n-\\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)\n\\right].\n\\label{eq:agentic-advantage}\n\\end{equation}\nThe first term is expected execution substitution: agentic output\nreplaces a share $\\lambda$ of the human's uncertain language-specific\noutput with agent execution $a z(A)$. The second is the verification and\ncompute cost of delegating. The third is risk substitution: delegation\nshrinks the variance attached to the human match but introduces residual\nagent-error risk. If $B>0$, delegation lowers the entry threshold for\nthe unfamiliar language, and by Assumption \\ref{ass:verification} the\nreduction is larger for higher-ability developers and more capable\nagents.",

        "id": "activation.band.unfamiliar.languages",
        "schema": 1,
        "semantic_claim": "Under the foothold assumption and a positive delegation advantage, the activity-indicator difference is exactly the opportunity interval from the delegation threshold through the solo threshold; a continuous conditional CDF gives the corresponding CDF difference, and summing weak threshold reductions gives nonnegative expected language-count expansion.",
        "source_claim_atom_semantic_sha256": "429bf0e60609a145128cc06273060aea262b3a706cb4c31f12df117e6d8b0bc7",
        "source_locator": "audit/source_archive_surface.tex:325-351",
        "source_quote": "\\begin{proposition}[Activation band for unfamiliar languages]\n\\label{prop:band}\nConsider an unfamiliar language satisfying Assumption \\ref{ass:foothold}.\nIf $B_{ik,t}>0$, then\n\\begin{equation}\nZ^2_{ik,t}-Z^1_{ik,t}\n=\n\\1{T^D_{ik,t}\\le\\omega_{ik,t}<T^S_{ik,t}}.\n\\label{eq:band-indicator}\n\\end{equation}\nIf the conditional opportunity CDF $F_{ik,t}$ is continuous, the\nprobability that delegation activates the language is\n$F_{ik,t}(T^S_{ik,t})-F_{ik,t}(T^D_{ik,t})$, and the expected\nlanguage-count expansion is\n\\begin{equation}\n\\E\\!\\left[N^2_{it}-N^1_{it}\\right]\n=\n\\sum_{k}\n\\left[\nF_{ik,t}\\!\\left(T^1_{ik,t}\\right)\n-\nF_{ik,t}\\!\\left(T^2_{ik,t}\\right)\n\\right]\n\\ge 0.\n\\label{eq:expected-count}\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{proposition}",
        "source_quote_sha256": "54e9535206e0095b63f6f83e3ef00b4e0545e33cc181535c9bb61a1b13a5988c"
      }

        "id": "dynamic.cumulative.language.effect",
        "schema": 1,
        "semantic_claim": "If every post-agent first-use hazard weakly exceeds its pre-agent hazard, the displayed expected cumulative-language gap is nonnegative; the source additionally claims strict increase and concavity whenever the old hazard is zero and the new hazard is positive.",
        "source_claim_atom_semantic_sha256": "368ddef758cc6879d7587c35f288330d60887aff0169d17d6d9cdf20c98f506e",
        "source_locator": "audit/source_archive_surface.tex:442-458",
        "source_quote": "\\begin{proposition}[Dynamic cumulative-language effect]\n\\label{prop:dynamic}\nFor an initially unfamiliar language, let $p^g_{ik}$ be the per-period\nfirst-use hazard under generation $g$. If $p^2_{ik}\\ge p^1_{ik}$, the\nexpected cumulative-language effect at event-time horizon $s$ is\n\\begin{equation}\n\\Delta C_i(s)\n=\n\\sum_{k\\in\\mathcal{U}_i}\n\\left[\n(1-p^1_{ik})^{s+1}-(1-p^2_{ik})^{s+1}\n\\right]\\ge0,\n\\label{eq:cumulative-gap}\n\\end{equation}\nwhich in the closed-frontier benchmark $p^1_{ik}=0<p^2_{ik}$ is strictly\nincreasing and concave over the observed horizon.\n\\end{proposition}",
        "source_quote_sha256": "643d5d3e6492a354a7ac3c708386d83298a5290bd89bb89acb291cc1702e1d9f"
      }
    ],

        "id": "specialist.and.ability.heterogeneity",
        "schema": 1,
        "semantic_claim": "Under comparable unfamiliar candidates, expected expansion equals the number of unfamiliar candidates times their common activation increment and increases with both candidate count and general ability.",
        "source_claim_atom_semantic_sha256": "4f195aae5865bf000620398455dbe86e411929a5f2f78e52b496bd012f8a479e",
        "source_locator": "audit/source_archive_surface.tex:621-634",
        "source_quote": "\\begin{proposition}[Specialist and ability heterogeneity]\n\\label{prop:specialist}\nUnder Assumption \\ref{ass:exchangeable}, expected expansion into initially\nunfamiliar languages is\n\\begin{equation}\n\\E[E_i\\mid a_i,U_i]=U_i p_i(a_i,A),\n\\qquad\nE_i\\equiv\\sum_{k\\in\\mathcal{U}_i}(Z^2_{ik}-Z^1_{ik}).\n\\label{eq:specialist-expansion}\n\\end{equation}\nIt is increasing in the stock of unfamiliar-language candidates $U_i$ and\nin general ability $a_i$. The largest extensive-margin gains accrue to\nhigh-ability specialists.\n\\end{proposition}",
        "source_quote_sha256": "f17c989de6190835917b666b5740a48d62824ef3ece21f1793396758e926a3c7"
      }

        "semantic_claim": "Conditionally independent Normal signals have total precision q and precision-weighted mean xbar_q; the displayed conjugate update sets posterior precision to prior precision plus q and posterior mean to the precision-weighted combination, so positive-variance nonempty signals raise precision.",
        "source_claim_atom_semantic_sha256": "4603f7abc1f889e2622d0e43ebf7b7e7906d9592e6ce048301fa9ccda7549a7d",
        "source_locator": "audit/source_archive_surface.tex:694-730",
        "source_quote": "\\subsection{Learning after agentic interaction}\n\nThe delegation channel explains why an unfamiliar language can be used\nimmediately; interaction with the agent and the language can also generate\nlearning that makes the language persist in the portfolio. Suppose the\ndeveloper observes signals\n\\begin{equation}\nx_{\\ell}=\\theta_{ik}+\\varepsilon_{\\ell},\n\\qquad\n\\varepsilon_{\\ell}\\sim\\N(0,\\sigma_{\\ell}^2),\n\\qquad\n\\ell=1,\\ldots,L,\n\\label{eq:signals}\n\\end{equation}\nconditionally independent given $\\theta_{ik}$. Let\n$q=\\sum_{\\ell=1}^L1/\\sigma_{\\ell}^2$ be the total signal precision and\n$\\bar{x}_q=(\\sum_{\\ell}x_\\ell/\\sigma_\\ell^2)/q$ the precision-weighted\nsignal mean. The posterior kernel is proportional to\n\\[\n\\exp\\left\\{\n-\\frac{1}{2}\\pi(\\theta-\\mu)^2\n-\\frac{1}{2}\\sum_{\\ell=1}^L\\frac{(x_\\ell-\\theta)^2}{\\sigma_\\ell^2}\n\\right\\},\n\\]\nand collecting terms in $\\theta$ gives the Bayesian update\n\\begin{equation}\n\\pi'_{ik}=\\pi_{ik}+q,\n\\qquad\n\\mu'_{ik}=\n\\frac{\\pi_{ik}\\mu_{ik}+q\\bar{x}_q}{\\pi_{ik}+q}.\n\\label{eq:bayes-update}\n\\end{equation}\nLearning raises precision and updates the productivity belief, so an\ninitially delegated language can remain active in later months. We use\nthis channel to interpret persistence and cumulative expansion, but not\nas the primary proof of immediate diversification: information can\nreveal bad matches as well as good ones.",
        "source_quote_sha256": "b6fea7eb4b2e6379a1d83103f29477ca1f74023fceb476765cf8a938bcfc0c06"
      }
    ],

      (∑ repository ∈ repositories,
          (opportunityLaw repository).real (Set.Ici (oldCost repository))) <
        ∑ repository ∈ repositories,
          (opportunityLaw repository).real (Set.Ici (newCost repository)))

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text:
The pre-agent menu is $\mathcal{M}_1=\{S,C\}$; agentic adoption expands it
to $\mathcal{M}_2=\{S,C,D\}$. Under generation $g$ the developer takes the
best available mode, $V^g_{ik,t}=\max_{m\in\mathcal{M}_g}V^m_{ik,t}$, and
language $k$ is \emph{active} when $Z^g_{ik,t}=\1{V^g_{ik,t}\ge0}$, so the
monthly language count is $N^g_{it}=\sum_k Z^g_{ik,t}$.

Because each surplus is affine in the opportunity shock $\omega$, each
mode has an activation threshold. Setting $V^S\ge0$ in Equation
\eqref{eq:solo-surplus}, solo production is viable when
\begin{equation}
\omega\ge
T^S\equiv b-s\mu+\frac{\rho s^2}{2\pi},
\label{eq:solo-threshold}
\end{equation}
and since $V^C=V^S+\gamma s-r_C$, augmentation is viable when
$\omega\ge T^C=T^S-(\gamma s-r_C)$. The developer takes whichever
pre-agent mode clears first, so the effective Generation-1 threshold is
\begin{equation}
T^1=\min\{T^S,T^C\}
=T^S-\max\{0,\gamma s-r_C\},
\label{eq:gen1-threshold}
\end{equation}
and for an unfamiliar language Assumption \ref{ass:foothold} implies
$\gamma s-r_C\le0$, hence $T^1=T^S$: augmentation does not move the
entry margin. Setting $V^D\ge0$ in Equation \eqref{eq:delegate-surplus},
delegation is viable when
\begin{align}
\omega\ge T^D
\equiv{}&
b-(1-\lambda)s\mu-\lambda a z(A)
+\kappa(a,s)+r_D
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(1-\lambda)^2s^2}{\pi}
+\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right],
\label{eq:delegate-threshold}
\end{align}
so the post-agent threshold is $T^2=\min\{T^1,T^D\}\le T^1$.

For an unfamiliar language, the economics reduce to the \emph{agentic
threshold reduction} $B\equiv T^1-T^D=T^S-T^D$. Differencing Equations
\eqref{eq:solo-threshold} and \eqref{eq:delegate-threshold} (algebra in
Appendix \ref{app:proofs}) gives
\begin{equation}
B
=
\lambda\bigl[a z(A)-s\mu\bigr]
-\kappa(a,s)-r_D
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(2\lambda-\lambda^2)s^2}{\pi}
-\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right].
\label{eq:agentic-advantage}
\end{equation}
The first term is expected execution substitution: agentic output
replaces a share $\lambda$ of the human's uncertain language-specific
output with agent execution $a z(A)$. The second is the verification and
compute cost of delegating. The third is risk substitution: delegation
shrinks the variance attached to the human match but introduces residual
agent-error risk. If $B>0$, delegation lowers the entry threshold for
the unfamiliar language, and by Assumption \ref{ass:verification} the
reduction is larger for higher-ability developers and more capable
agents.

There are developers $i$, programming languages $k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$, and
months $t$. Developer $i$ has a familiar-language set $\mathcal{K}_i$ and
an unfamiliar set $\mathcal{U}_i$ with $U_i\equiv|\mathcal{U}_i|$; a
specialist is a developer with small $|\mathcal{K}_i|$ and therefore many
unfamiliar candidates. Empirically, ``unfamiliar'' means not observed in
the developer's prior public GitHub contributions; it need not imply
that the developer has no private experience with the language. For each developer--language pair, $s_{ik,t}\in[0,1]$
is language-specific execution skill, and the developer holds Normal
beliefs $\theta_{ik}\sim\N(\mu_{ik,t},1/\pi_{ik,t})$ about her latent
productivity match, with low skill and low precision in unfamiliar
languages. General ability $a_i\ge0$ --- the capacity to specify,
decompose, and verify a task --- is language-invariant. Each language-month
carries an opportunity value $\omega_{ik,t}$ and an activation cost
$b_{ik,t}$. The developer has CARA utility with coefficient $\rho$, so a
payoff with mean $m$ and variance $\sigma^2$ has certainty equivalent
$m-\rho\sigma^2/2$ (Appendix \ref{app:proofs}).

Suppressing $(i,k,t)$ subscripts, the three modes deliver net
certainty-equivalent surpluses
\begin{align}
V^S &= \omega+s\mu-\frac{\rho s^2}{2\pi}-b,
\label{eq:solo-surplus}\\
V^C &= V^S+\gamma s-r_C,
\label{eq:copilot-surplus}\\
V^D &= \omega+(1-\lambda)s\mu+\lambda a z(A)
-\kappa(a,s)-r_D-b
-\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(1-\lambda)^2s^2}{\pi}
+\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right].
\label{eq:delegate-surplus}
\end{align}
Solo production exposes the developer to uncertainty about her own match.
Generation-1 augmentation yields a deterministic gain $\gamma s$
proportional to existing skill, net of interaction cost $r_C$: the
developer benefits most when she can read, adapt, and verify the
suggestion herself. Generation-2 delegation hands a share
$\lambda\in(0,1]$ of execution to an agent with competence $z(A)$,
increasing in capability $A$ and scaled by the developer's general
ability; it carries verification cost $\kappa(a,s)$, compute cost $r_D$,
and residual error variance $\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)$, while shrinking the
variance attached to the human match from $s^2/\pi$ to
$(1-\lambda)^2 s^2/\pi$.

The pre-agent menu is $\mathcal{M}_1=\{S,C\}$; agentic adoption expands it
to $\mathcal{M}_2=\{S,C,D\}$. Under generation $g$ the developer takes the
best available mode, $V^g_{ik,t}=\max_{m\in\mathcal{M}_g}V^m_{ik,t}$, and
language $k$ is \emph{active} when $Z^g_{ik,t}=\1{V^g_{ik,t}\ge0}$, so the
monthly language count is $N^g_{it}=\sum_k Z^g_{ik,t}$.

\begin{assumption}[Comparable unfamiliar-language candidates]
\label{ass:exchangeable}
Conditional on developer characteristics such as general ability, all
unfamiliar languages have the same per-language activation increment
$p_i(a_i,A)\ge0$, and $p_i$ is increasing in $a_i$ whenever Assumption
\ref{ass:verification} makes delegation thresholds fall with ability.
\end{assumption}

dimensions.required_check: Compare every expanded Lean binder domain, result quantifier, and proposition against the literal source statement. Check direction, scope, endpoint, and fixed-versus-uniform quantification; alpha-renaming is not a semantic change. For every formula used as a transformed density, likelihood, kernel, or probability law, check its sign, normalization, and Jacobian factor across the entire declared parameter domain. An algebraic scaling formula is not a probability-law conclusion outside the domain where those facts are proved.

Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. An arbitrary carrier or a silently strengthened finite carrier needs a source anchor or a checked bridge. When an expanded finite carrier encodes a source cardinal parameter through index arithmetic such as Fin (n + c), state the source parameter, the Lean expression, and a proved translation; local type names and inferred cardinality are not evidence. When a strict conclusion needs distinct, non-endpoint, or interior carrier elements, derive the exact cardinality threshold and witness from the source; a bare source phrase such as 'n candidates' does not supply N >= 3. When the generated surface requests a cardinality-boundary analysis, record the source and Lean cardinal domains, every smallest/endpoint case checked, and either the strictness witness or a semantic reason no such witness is needed. A theorem, wrapper, or carrier name is not that analysis. A local opaque/constant/axiom carrier must expose a checked refinement before it is treated as ordinary model data.

For a finite/ordered probabilistic model, derive support at each endpoint from the source condition actually stated. Strict adjacent-tail comparisons do not by themselves supply a terminal cutoff or positive top/bottom atom; inspect zero mass, degenerate, and boundary cases separately.

Identify the source stochastic process and the Lean joint law separately. Do not replace a source state recurrence, conditioning rule, or time-indexed law with an iid/product construction without a Lean-checked equality, simulation, or refinement from the source primitives. If either side sorts, ranks, relabels, or quotients samples before computing an outcome, prove the corresponding pushforward and outcome-equivariance bridge; matching marginal tables or an informal exchangeability argument is not enough. When the generated surface requests transformed-law analysis, record the source and Lean operations, the full parameter domain including sign/zero endpoints, normalization or pushforward evidence, and outcome-equivariance evidence (or an explicit semantic no-transform/no-relabeling finding). Separately write the source and Lean distribution parameterizations: the exact scale/rate/precision/standard-deviation/variance convention, the parameter mapping formula, and a checked law equality or outcome-preservation bridge. A positive reparameterization or matching declaration name is not a law-equivalence argument. When a standard Measure/Kernel carrier transport is present, identify the source carrier and the Lean carrier, show whether every stage is one joint draw or a source-defined conditional kernel composition, and classify the measure as a source pushforward, source conditioning/restriction, source-defined joint kernel law, generated product/kernel measure, or weighted/tilted measure. A weighted likelihood measure is not a source pushforward without an explicit transport theorem. A rate-free or rate-indexed source claim needs a checked rate-indexed family bridge, not one selected Lean rate. When the elaborated surface contains a ReflTransGen path and a relation-valued state transition, identify the concrete source executor, initial/terminal states, and transition relation; a caller-supplied trace, serialization, or refinement package requires its own checked construction from source primitives.

State exactly whether source and Lean use a pointwise conditional law, an almost-everywhere conditional version, positive-fiber identities, or measurable-event calibration. Expand the event, sigma-algebra/measurability, and joint-law formula; a statement about exact fibers does not silently determine atomless or null fibers. Any switch among these semantics needs a Lean-checked bridge, not a source-looking conditional-probability or calibration name.

For every source or Lean expectation/integral reached through this model, identify the law and integrand and establish the exact definedness convention: measurability or a.e.-measurability, integrability/finite integral, or an explicitly extended-value integral. A displayed E[...] is not a total Real number merely because a predictor or classifier was named; indicator and strategy correctness functions require their own measurability/integrability bridge.

For every conditioning/partition formula reached through this model, compare finite, countable, and arbitrary partition scope; cell measurability, disjointness, and cover on the relevant support; and the value assigned when a cell has zero mass. Expand every ratio/branch used to totalize zero denominators. A finite measurable-cell proof or a positive-mass-only identity does not cover an advertised arbitrary partition without a Lean-checked refinement.

Compare the source rate codomain with the Lean codomain after unfolding the rate definition. A Real-valued formula is not automatically a WithTop/extended-real statement: account for eventual-zero events, infinite rates, zero sample counts, and boundary minimizers.

        verificationCost ability skill - delegationCost - activationCost -

            residualVariance ability skill capability)

source_claim_atom_contexts.semantic_claim: The source model assigns skill, general ability, opportunity, activation cost, CARA risk aversion, and Normal productivity beliefs, then defines the solo, conversational-assistant, and delegation certainty-equivalent surpluses by Equations (1)-(3).
source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
There are developers $i$, programming languages $k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$, and
months $t$. Developer $i$ has a familiar-language set $\mathcal{K}_i$ and
an unfamiliar set $\mathcal{U}_i$ with $U_i\equiv|\mathcal{U}_i|$; a
specialist is a developer with small $|\mathcal{K}_i|$ and therefore many
unfamiliar candidates. Empirically, ``unfamiliar'' means not observed in
the developer's prior public GitHub contributions; it need not imply
that the developer has no private experience with the language. For each developer--language pair, $s_{ik,t}\in[0,1]$
is language-specific execution skill, and the developer holds Normal
beliefs $\theta_{ik}\sim\N(\mu_{ik,t},1/\pi_{ik,t})$ about her latent
productivity match, with low skill and low precision in unfamiliar
languages. General ability $a_i\ge0$ --- the capacity to specify,
decompose, and verify a task --- is language-invariant. Each language-month
carries an opportunity value $\omega_{ik,t}$ and an activation cost
$b_{ik,t}$. The developer has CARA utility with coefficient $\rho$, so a
payoff with mean $m$ and variance $\sigma^2$ has certainty equivalent
$m-\rho\sigma^2/2$ (Appendix \ref{app:proofs}).

Suppressing $(i,k,t)$ subscripts, the three modes deliver net
certainty-equivalent surpluses
\begin{align}
V^S &= \omega+s\mu-\frac{\rho s^2}{2\pi}-b,
\label{eq:solo-surplus}\\
V^C &= V^S+\gamma s-r_C,
\label{eq:copilot-surplus}\\
V^D &= \omega+(1-\lambda)s\mu+\lambda a z(A)
-\kappa(a,s)-r_D-b
-\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(1-\lambda)^2s^2}{\pi}
+\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right].
\label{eq:delegate-surplus}
\end{align}
Solo production exposes the developer to uncertainty about her own match.
Generation-1 augmentation yields a deterministic gain $\gamma s$
proportional to existing skill, net of interaction cost $r_C$: the
developer benefits most when she can read, adapt, and verify the
suggestion herself. Generation-2 delegation hands a share
$\lambda\in(0,1]$ of execution to an agent with competence $z(A)$,
increasing in capability $A$ and scaled by the developer's general
ability; it carries verification cost $\kappa(a,s)$, compute cost $r_D$,
and residual error variance $\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)$, while shrinking the
variance attached to the human match from $s^2/\pi$ to
$(1-\lambda)^2 s^2/\pi$.

source_claim_atom_contexts.semantic_claim: Equations (4)-(8) define the solo, conversational, Generation-1, delegation, and Generation-2 activation thresholds and the unfamiliar-language delegation advantage B, including the foothold consequence T1 = TS.
source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
Because each surplus is affine in the opportunity shock $\omega$, each
mode has an activation threshold. Setting $V^S\ge0$ in Equation
\eqref{eq:solo-surplus}, solo production is viable when
\begin{equation}
\omega\ge
T^S\equiv b-s\mu+\frac{\rho s^2}{2\pi},
\label{eq:solo-threshold}
\end{equation}
and since $V^C=V^S+\gamma s-r_C$, augmentation is viable when
$\omega\ge T^C=T^S-(\gamma s-r_C)$. The developer takes whichever
pre-agent mode clears first, so the effective Generation-1 threshold is
\begin{equation}
T^1=\min\{T^S,T^C\}
=T^S-\max\{0,\gamma s-r_C\},
\label{eq:gen1-threshold}
\end{equation}
and for an unfamiliar language Assumption \ref{ass:foothold} implies
$\gamma s-r_C\le0$, hence $T^1=T^S$: augmentation does not move the
entry margin. Setting $V^D\ge0$ in Equation \eqref{eq:delegate-surplus},
delegation is viable when
\begin{align}
\omega\ge T^D
\equiv{}&
b-(1-\lambda)s\mu-\lambda a z(A)
+\kappa(a,s)+r_D
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(1-\lambda)^2s^2}{\pi}
+\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right],
\label{eq:delegate-threshold}
\end{align}
so the post-agent threshold is $T^2=\min\{T^1,T^D\}\le T^1$.

For an unfamiliar language, the economics reduce to the \emph{agentic
threshold reduction} $B\equiv T^1-T^D=T^S-T^D$. Differencing Equations
\eqref{eq:solo-threshold} and \eqref{eq:delegate-threshold} (algebra in
Appendix \ref{app:proofs}) gives
\begin{equation}
B
=
\lambda\bigl[a z(A)-s\mu\bigr]
-\kappa(a,s)-r_D
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(2\lambda-\lambda^2)s^2}{\pi}
-\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right].
\label{eq:agentic-advantage}
\end{equation}
The first term is expected execution substitution: agentic output
replaces a share $\lambda$ of the human's uncertain language-specific
output with agent execution $a z(A)$. The second is the verification and
compute cost of delegating. The third is risk substitution: delegation
shrinks the variance attached to the human match but introduces residual
agent-error risk. If $B>0$, delegation lowers the entry threshold for
the unfamiliar language, and by Assumption \ref{ass:verification} the
reduction is larger for higher-ability developers and more capable
agents.

theorem dynamic_cumulative_language_effect : dynamic_cumulative_language_effectSpec := by
  intro Language unfamiliar oldHazard newHazard horizon
  dsimp only
  intro hold_nonneg hnew_le_one hhazard
  constructor
  · exact cumulative_gap_nonneg unfamiliar oldHazard newHazard horizon
      hold_nonneg hnew_le_one hhazard
  · intro hne hold_zero hnew_pos hnew_lt_one
    have hgap (eventTime : ℕ) :
        (∑ language ∈ unfamiliar,
            ((1 - oldHazard language) ^ (eventTime + 1) -
              (1 - newHazard language) ^ (eventTime + 1))) =
          ∑ language ∈ unfamiliar,
            (1 - (1 - newHazard language) ^ (eventTime + 1)) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro language hlanguage
      rw [hold_zero language hlanguage]
      norm_num
    constructor
    · rw [hgap horizon, hgap (horizon + 1)]
      simpa only [Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_left_comm] using
        closed_frontier_gap_strict_mono unfamiliar newHazard hne hnew_pos
          hnew_lt_one horizon
    · rw [hgap (horizon + 2), hgap (horizon + 1), hgap horizon]
      simpa only [Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_left_comm] using
        closed_frontier_gap_strict_concave unfamiliar newHazard hne hnew_pos
          hnew_lt_one horizon

source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
\subsection{Learning after agentic interaction}

The delegation channel explains why an unfamiliar language can be used
immediately; interaction with the agent and the language can also generate
learning that makes the language persist in the portfolio. Suppose the
developer observes signals
\begin{equation}
x_{\ell}=\theta_{ik}+\varepsilon_{\ell},
\qquad
\varepsilon_{\ell}\sim\N(0,\sigma_{\ell}^2),
\qquad
\ell=1,\ldots,L,
\label{eq:signals}
\end{equation}
conditionally independent given $\theta_{ik}$. Let
$q=\sum_{\ell=1}^L1/\sigma_{\ell}^2$ be the total signal precision and
$\bar{x}_q=(\sum_{\ell}x_\ell/\sigma_\ell^2)/q$ the precision-weighted
signal mean. The posterior kernel is proportional to
\[
\exp\left\{
-\frac{1}{2}\pi(\theta-\mu)^2
-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\frac{(x_\ell-\theta)^2}{\sigma_\ell^2}
\right\},
\]
and collecting terms in $\theta$ gives the Bayesian update
\begin{equation}
\pi'_{ik}=\pi_{ik}+q,
\qquad
\mu'_{ik}=
\frac{\pi_{ik}\mu_{ik}+q\bar{x}_q}{\pi_{ik}+q}.
\label{eq:bayes-update}
\end{equation}
Learning raises precision and updates the productivity belief, so an
initially delegated language can remain active in later months. We use
this channel to interpret persistence and cumulative expansion, but not
as the primary proof of immediate diversification: information can
reveal bad matches as well as good ones.

source_claim_atom_contexts.semantic_claim: If repository entry cost weakly falls when its required language can be activated and delegation weakly expands the active-language set, expected repository access weakly increases; the source statement claims strict increase when some repositories require languages in the activation band.
source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
\begin{proposition}[Repository expansion]
\label{prop:repos}
Suppose each repository requires at least one programming language and carries
an entry cost that is weakly decreasing when the developer can activate that
language. If agentic delegation weakly expands the active-language set, then
the expected number of repositories the developer can contribute to weakly
increases. It increases strictly when some repositories require languages in
the delegation activation band.
\end{proposition}

def dynamic_cumulative_language_effectSpec : Prop := ∀ {Language : Type*} (unfamiliar : Finset Language)
      (oldHazard newHazard : Language → ℝ) (horizon : ℕ),
    let cumulativeGap : ℕ → ℝ := fun eventTime =>

        ((1 - oldHazard language) ^ (eventTime + 1) -
          (1 - newHazard language) ^ (eventTime + 1))
    (∀ language ∈ unfamiliar, 0 ≤ oldHazard language) →
    (∀ language ∈ unfamiliar, newHazard language ≤ 1) →
    (∀ language ∈ unfamiliar, oldHazard language ≤ newHazard language) →
    0 ≤ cumulativeGap horizon ∧

        (∀ language ∈ unfamiliar, oldHazard language = 0) →
        (∀ language ∈ unfamiliar, 0 < newHazard language) →
        (∀ language ∈ unfamiliar, newHazard language < 1) →

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text:
The pre-agent menu is $\mathcal{M}_1=\{S,C\}$; agentic adoption expands it
to $\mathcal{M}_2=\{S,C,D\}$. Under generation $g$ the developer takes the
best available mode, $V^g_{ik,t}=\max_{m\in\mathcal{M}_g}V^m_{ik,t}$, and
language $k$ is \emph{active} when $Z^g_{ik,t}=\1{V^g_{ik,t}\ge0}$, so the
monthly language count is $N^g_{it}=\sum_k Z^g_{ik,t}$.

Because each surplus is affine in the opportunity shock $\omega$, each
mode has an activation threshold. Setting $V^S\ge0$ in Equation
\eqref{eq:solo-surplus}, solo production is viable when
\begin{equation}
\omega\ge
T^S\equiv b-s\mu+\frac{\rho s^2}{2\pi},
\label{eq:solo-threshold}
\end{equation}
and since $V^C=V^S+\gamma s-r_C$, augmentation is viable when
$\omega\ge T^C=T^S-(\gamma s-r_C)$. The developer takes whichever
pre-agent mode clears first, so the effective Generation-1 threshold is
\begin{equation}
T^1=\min\{T^S,T^C\}
=T^S-\max\{0,\gamma s-r_C\},
\label{eq:gen1-threshold}
\end{equation}
and for an unfamiliar language Assumption \ref{ass:foothold} implies
$\gamma s-r_C\le0$, hence $T^1=T^S$: augmentation does not move the
entry margin. Setting $V^D\ge0$ in Equation \eqref{eq:delegate-surplus},
delegation is viable when
\begin{align}
\omega\ge T^D
\equiv{}&
b-(1-\lambda)s\mu-\lambda a z(A)
+\kappa(a,s)+r_D
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(1-\lambda)^2s^2}{\pi}
+\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right],
\label{eq:delegate-threshold}
\end{align}
so the post-agent threshold is $T^2=\min\{T^1,T^D\}\le T^1$.

For an unfamiliar language, the economics reduce to the \emph{agentic
threshold reduction} $B\equiv T^1-T^D=T^S-T^D$. Differencing Equations
\eqref{eq:solo-threshold} and \eqref{eq:delegate-threshold} (algebra in
Appendix \ref{app:proofs}) gives
\begin{equation}
B
=
\lambda\bigl[a z(A)-s\mu\bigr]
-\kappa(a,s)-r_D
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(2\lambda-\lambda^2)s^2}{\pi}
-\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right].
\label{eq:agentic-advantage}
\end{equation}
The first term is expected execution substitution: agentic output
replaces a share $\lambda$ of the human's uncertain language-specific
output with agent execution $a z(A)$. The second is the verification and
compute cost of delegating. The third is risk substitution: delegation
shrinks the variance attached to the human match but introduces residual
agent-error risk. If $B>0$, delegation lowers the entry threshold for
the unfamiliar language, and by Assumption \ref{ass:verification} the
reduction is larger for higher-ability developers and more capable
agents.

There are developers $i$, programming languages $k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$, and
months $t$. Developer $i$ has a familiar-language set $\mathcal{K}_i$ and
an unfamiliar set $\mathcal{U}_i$ with $U_i\equiv|\mathcal{U}_i|$; a
specialist is a developer with small $|\mathcal{K}_i|$ and therefore many
unfamiliar candidates. Empirically, ``unfamiliar'' means not observed in
the developer's prior public GitHub contributions; it need not imply
that the developer has no private experience with the language. For each developer--language pair, $s_{ik,t}\in[0,1]$
is language-specific execution skill, and the developer holds Normal
beliefs $\theta_{ik}\sim\N(\mu_{ik,t},1/\pi_{ik,t})$ about her latent
productivity match, with low skill and low precision in unfamiliar
languages. General ability $a_i\ge0$ --- the capacity to specify,
decompose, and verify a task --- is language-invariant. Each language-month
carries an opportunity value $\omega_{ik,t}$ and an activation cost
$b_{ik,t}$. The developer has CARA utility with coefficient $\rho$, so a
payoff with mean $m$ and variance $\sigma^2$ has certainty equivalent
$m-\rho\sigma^2/2$ (Appendix \ref{app:proofs}).

Suppressing $(i,k,t)$ subscripts, the three modes deliver net
certainty-equivalent surpluses
\begin{align}
V^S &= \omega+s\mu-\frac{\rho s^2}{2\pi}-b,
\label{eq:solo-surplus}\\
V^C &= V^S+\gamma s-r_C,
\label{eq:copilot-surplus}\\
V^D &= \omega+(1-\lambda)s\mu+\lambda a z(A)
-\kappa(a,s)-r_D-b
-\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(1-\lambda)^2s^2}{\pi}
+\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right].
\label{eq:delegate-surplus}
\end{align}
Solo production exposes the developer to uncertainty about her own match.
Generation-1 augmentation yields a deterministic gain $\gamma s$
proportional to existing skill, net of interaction cost $r_C$: the
developer benefits most when she can read, adapt, and verify the
suggestion herself. Generation-2 delegation hands a share
$\lambda\in(0,1]$ of execution to an agent with competence $z(A)$,
increasing in capability $A$ and scaled by the developer's general
ability; it carries verification cost $\kappa(a,s)$, compute cost $r_D$,
and residual error variance $\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)$, while shrinking the
variance attached to the human match from $s^2/\pi$ to
$(1-\lambda)^2 s^2/\pi$.

The pre-agent menu is $\mathcal{M}_1=\{S,C\}$; agentic adoption expands it
to $\mathcal{M}_2=\{S,C,D\}$. Under generation $g$ the developer takes the
best available mode, $V^g_{ik,t}=\max_{m\in\mathcal{M}_g}V^m_{ik,t}$, and
language $k$ is \emph{active} when $Z^g_{ik,t}=\1{V^g_{ik,t}\ge0}$, so the
monthly language count is $N^g_{it}=\sum_k Z^g_{ik,t}$.

\begin{assumption}[Comparable unfamiliar-language candidates]
\label{ass:exchangeable}
Conditional on developer characteristics such as general ability, all
unfamiliar languages have the same per-language activation increment
$p_i(a_i,A)\ge0$, and $p_i$ is increasing in $a_i$ whenever Assumption
\ref{ass:verification} makes delegation thresholds fall with ability.
\end{assumption}

dimensions.required_check: Compare every expanded Lean binder domain, result quantifier, and proposition against the literal source statement. Check direction, scope, endpoint, and fixed-versus-uniform quantification; alpha-renaming is not a semantic change. For every formula used as a transformed density, likelihood, kernel, or probability law, check its sign, normalization, and Jacobian factor across the entire declared parameter domain. An algebraic scaling formula is not a probability-law conclusion outside the domain where those facts are proved.

Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. An arbitrary carrier or a silently strengthened finite carrier needs a source anchor or a checked bridge. When an expanded finite carrier encodes a source cardinal parameter through index arithmetic such as Fin (n + c), state the source parameter, the Lean expression, and a proved translation; local type names and inferred cardinality are not evidence. When a strict conclusion needs distinct, non-endpoint, or interior carrier elements, derive the exact cardinality threshold and witness from the source; a bare source phrase such as 'n candidates' does not supply N >= 3. When the generated surface requests a cardinality-boundary analysis, record the source and Lean cardinal domains, every smallest/endpoint case checked, and either the strictness witness or a semantic reason no such witness is needed. A theorem, wrapper, or carrier name is not that analysis. A local opaque/constant/axiom carrier must expose a checked refinement before it is treated as ordinary model data.

For a finite/ordered probabilistic model, derive support at each endpoint from the source condition actually stated. Strict adjacent-tail comparisons do not by themselves supply a terminal cutoff or positive top/bottom atom; inspect zero mass, degenerate, and boundary cases separately.

Identify the source stochastic process and the Lean joint law separately. Do not replace a source state recurrence, conditioning rule, or time-indexed law with an iid/product construction without a Lean-checked equality, simulation, or refinement from the source primitives. If either side sorts, ranks, relabels, or quotients samples before computing an outcome, prove the corresponding pushforward and outcome-equivariance bridge; matching marginal tables or an informal exchangeability argument is not enough. When the generated surface requests transformed-law analysis, record the source and Lean operations, the full parameter domain including sign/zero endpoints, normalization or pushforward evidence, and outcome-equivariance evidence (or an explicit semantic no-transform/no-relabeling finding). Separately write the source and Lean distribution parameterizations: the exact scale/rate/precision/standard-deviation/variance convention, the parameter mapping formula, and a checked law equality or outcome-preservation bridge. A positive reparameterization or matching declaration name is not a law-equivalence argument. When a standard Measure/Kernel carrier transport is present, identify the source carrier and the Lean carrier, show whether every stage is one joint draw or a source-defined conditional kernel composition, and classify the measure as a source pushforward, source conditioning/restriction, source-defined joint kernel law, generated product/kernel measure, or weighted/tilted measure. A weighted likelihood measure is not a source pushforward without an explicit transport theorem. A rate-free or rate-indexed source claim needs a checked rate-indexed family bridge, not one selected Lean rate. When the elaborated surface contains a ReflTransGen path and a relation-valued state transition, identify the concrete source executor, initial/terminal states, and transition relation; a caller-supplied trace, serialization, or refinement package requires its own checked construction from source primitives.

State exactly whether source and Lean use a pointwise conditional law, an almost-everywhere conditional version, positive-fiber identities, or measurable-event calibration. Expand the event, sigma-algebra/measurability, and joint-law formula; a statement about exact fibers does not silently determine atomless or null fibers. Any switch among these semantics needs a Lean-checked bridge, not a source-looking conditional-probability or calibration name.

For every source or Lean expectation/integral reached through this model, identify the law and integrand and establish the exact definedness convention: measurability or a.e.-measurability, integrability/finite integral, or an explicitly extended-value integral. A displayed E[...] is not a total Real number merely because a predictor or classifier was named; indicator and strategy correctness functions require their own measurability/integrability bridge.

For every conditioning/partition formula reached through this model, compare finite, countable, and arbitrary partition scope; cell measurability, disjointness, and cover on the relevant support; and the value assigned when a cell has zero mass. Expand every ratio/branch used to totalize zero denominators. A finite measurable-cell proof or a positive-mass-only identity does not cover an advertised arbitrary partition without a Lean-checked refinement.

Compare the source rate codomain with the Lean codomain after unfolding the rate definition. A Real-valued formula is not automatically a WithTop/extended-real statement: account for eventual-zero events, infinite rates, zero sample counts, and boundary minimizers.

source_claim_atom_contexts.semantic_claim: The source model assigns skill, general ability, opportunity, activation cost, CARA risk aversion, and Normal productivity beliefs, then defines the solo, conversational-assistant, and delegation certainty-equivalent surpluses by Equations (1)-(3).
source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
There are developers $i$, programming languages $k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$, and
months $t$. Developer $i$ has a familiar-language set $\mathcal{K}_i$ and
an unfamiliar set $\mathcal{U}_i$ with $U_i\equiv|\mathcal{U}_i|$; a
specialist is a developer with small $|\mathcal{K}_i|$ and therefore many
unfamiliar candidates. Empirically, ``unfamiliar'' means not observed in
the developer's prior public GitHub contributions; it need not imply
that the developer has no private experience with the language. For each developer--language pair, $s_{ik,t}\in[0,1]$
is language-specific execution skill, and the developer holds Normal
beliefs $\theta_{ik}\sim\N(\mu_{ik,t},1/\pi_{ik,t})$ about her latent
productivity match, with low skill and low precision in unfamiliar
languages. General ability $a_i\ge0$ --- the capacity to specify,
decompose, and verify a task --- is language-invariant. Each language-month
carries an opportunity value $\omega_{ik,t}$ and an activation cost
$b_{ik,t}$. The developer has CARA utility with coefficient $\rho$, so a
payoff with mean $m$ and variance $\sigma^2$ has certainty equivalent
$m-\rho\sigma^2/2$ (Appendix \ref{app:proofs}).

Suppressing $(i,k,t)$ subscripts, the three modes deliver net
certainty-equivalent surpluses
\begin{align}
V^S &= \omega+s\mu-\frac{\rho s^2}{2\pi}-b,
\label{eq:solo-surplus}\\
V^C &= V^S+\gamma s-r_C,
\label{eq:copilot-surplus}\\
V^D &= \omega+(1-\lambda)s\mu+\lambda a z(A)
-\kappa(a,s)-r_D-b
-\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(1-\lambda)^2s^2}{\pi}
+\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right].
\label{eq:delegate-surplus}
\end{align}
Solo production exposes the developer to uncertainty about her own match.
Generation-1 augmentation yields a deterministic gain $\gamma s$
proportional to existing skill, net of interaction cost $r_C$: the
developer benefits most when she can read, adapt, and verify the
suggestion herself. Generation-2 delegation hands a share
$\lambda\in(0,1]$ of execution to an agent with competence $z(A)$,
increasing in capability $A$ and scaled by the developer's general
ability; it carries verification cost $\kappa(a,s)$, compute cost $r_D$,
and residual error variance $\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)$, while shrinking the
variance attached to the human match from $s^2/\pi$ to
$(1-\lambda)^2 s^2/\pi$.

The pre-agent menu is $\mathcal{M}_1=\{S,C\}$; agentic adoption expands it
to $\mathcal{M}_2=\{S,C,D\}$. Under generation $g$ the developer takes the
best available mode, $V^g_{ik,t}=\max_{m\in\mathcal{M}_g}V^m_{ik,t}$, and
language $k$ is \emph{active} when $Z^g_{ik,t}=\1{V^g_{ik,t}\ge0}$, so the
monthly language count is $N^g_{it}=\sum_k Z^g_{ik,t}$.

source_claim_atom_contexts.semantic_claim: Equations (4)-(8) define the solo, conversational, Generation-1, delegation, and Generation-2 activation thresholds and the unfamiliar-language delegation advantage B, including the foothold consequence T1 = TS.
source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
Because each surplus is affine in the opportunity shock $\omega$, each
mode has an activation threshold. Setting $V^S\ge0$ in Equation
\eqref{eq:solo-surplus}, solo production is viable when
\begin{equation}
\omega\ge
T^S\equiv b-s\mu+\frac{\rho s^2}{2\pi},
\label{eq:solo-threshold}
\end{equation}
and since $V^C=V^S+\gamma s-r_C$, augmentation is viable when
$\omega\ge T^C=T^S-(\gamma s-r_C)$. The developer takes whichever
pre-agent mode clears first, so the effective Generation-1 threshold is
\begin{equation}
T^1=\min\{T^S,T^C\}
=T^S-\max\{0,\gamma s-r_C\},
\label{eq:gen1-threshold}
\end{equation}
and for an unfamiliar language Assumption \ref{ass:foothold} implies
$\gamma s-r_C\le0$, hence $T^1=T^S$: augmentation does not move the
entry margin. Setting $V^D\ge0$ in Equation \eqref{eq:delegate-surplus},
delegation is viable when
\begin{align}
\omega\ge T^D
\equiv{}&
b-(1-\lambda)s\mu-\lambda a z(A)
+\kappa(a,s)+r_D
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(1-\lambda)^2s^2}{\pi}
+\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right],
\label{eq:delegate-threshold}
\end{align}
so the post-agent threshold is $T^2=\min\{T^1,T^D\}\le T^1$.

For an unfamiliar language, the economics reduce to the \emph{agentic
threshold reduction} $B\equiv T^1-T^D=T^S-T^D$. Differencing Equations
\eqref{eq:solo-threshold} and \eqref{eq:delegate-threshold} (algebra in
Appendix \ref{app:proofs}) gives
\begin{equation}
B
=
\lambda\bigl[a z(A)-s\mu\bigr]
-\kappa(a,s)-r_D
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(2\lambda-\lambda^2)s^2}{\pi}
-\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right].
\label{eq:agentic-advantage}
\end{equation}
The first term is expected execution substitution: agentic output
replaces a share $\lambda$ of the human's uncertain language-specific
output with agent execution $a z(A)$. The second is the verification and
compute cost of delegating. The third is risk substitution: delegation
shrinks the variance attached to the human match but introduces residual
agent-error risk. If $B>0$, delegation lowers the entry threshold for
the unfamiliar language, and by Assumption \ref{ass:verification} the
reduction is larger for higher-ability developers and more capable
agents.

dimensions.required_check: Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. An arbitrary carrier or a silently strengthened finite carrier needs a source anchor or a checked bridge. When an expanded finite carrier encodes a source cardinal parameter through index arithmetic such as Fin (n + c), state the source parameter, the Lean expression, and a proved translation; local type names and inferred cardinality are not evidence. When a strict conclusion needs distinct, non-endpoint, or interior carrier elements, derive the exact cardinality threshold and witness from the source; a bare source phrase such as 'n candidates' does not supply N >= 3. When the generated surface requests a cardinality-boundary analysis, record the source and Lean cardinal domains, every smallest/endpoint case checked, and either the strictness witness or a semantic reason no such witness is needed. A theorem, wrapper, or carrier name is not that analysis. A local opaque/constant/axiom carrier must expose a checked refinement before it is treated as ordinary model data.

For a finite/ordered probabilistic model, derive support at each endpoint from the source condition actually stated. Strict adjacent-tail comparisons do not by themselves supply a terminal cutoff or positive top/bottom atom; inspect zero mass, degenerate, and boundary cases separately.

Identify the source stochastic process and the Lean joint law separately. Do not replace a source state recurrence, conditioning rule, or time-indexed law with an iid/product construction without a Lean-checked equality, simulation, or refinement from the source primitives. If either side sorts, ranks, relabels, or quotients samples before computing an outcome, prove the corresponding pushforward and outcome-equivariance bridge; matching marginal tables or an informal exchangeability argument is not enough. When the generated surface requests transformed-law analysis, record the source and Lean operations, the full parameter domain including sign/zero endpoints, normalization or pushforward evidence, and outcome-equivariance evidence (or an explicit semantic no-transform/no-relabeling finding). Separately write the source and Lean distribution parameterizations: the exact scale/rate/precision/standard-deviation/variance convention, the parameter mapping formula, and a checked law equality or outcome-preservation bridge. A positive reparameterization or matching declaration name is not a law-equivalence argument. When a standard Measure/Kernel carrier transport is present, identify the source carrier and the Lean carrier, show whether every stage is one joint draw or a source-defined conditional kernel composition, and classify the measure as a source pushforward, source conditioning/restriction, source-defined joint kernel law, generated product/kernel measure, or weighted/tilted measure. A weighted likelihood measure is not a source pushforward without an explicit transport theorem. A rate-free or rate-indexed source claim needs a checked rate-indexed family bridge, not one selected Lean rate. When the elaborated surface contains a ReflTransGen path and a relation-valued state transition, identify the concrete source executor, initial/terminal states, and transition relation; a caller-supplied trace, serialization, or refinement package requires its own checked construction from source primitives.

State exactly whether source and Lean use a pointwise conditional law, an almost-everywhere conditional version, positive-fiber identities, or measurable-event calibration. Expand the event, sigma-algebra/measurability, and joint-law formula; a statement about exact fibers does not silently determine atomless or null fibers. Any switch among these semantics needs a Lean-checked bridge, not a source-looking conditional-probability or calibration name.

For every source or Lean expectation/integral reached through this model, identify the law and integrand and establish the exact definedness convention: measurability or a.e.-measurability, integrability/finite integral, or an explicitly extended-value integral. A displayed E[...] is not a total Real number merely because a predictor or classifier was named; indicator and strategy correctness functions require their own measurability/integrability bridge.

Expand every ratio/branch used to totalize zero denominators. A finite measurable-cell proof or a positive-mass-only identity does not cover an advertised arbitrary partition without a Lean-checked refinement.

Compare the source rate codomain with the Lean codomain after unfolding the rate definition. A Real-valued formula is not automatically a WithTop/extended-real statement: account for eventual-zero events, infinite rates, zero sample counts, and boundary minimizers.

source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
\subsection{Learning after agentic interaction}

The delegation channel explains why an unfamiliar language can be used
immediately; interaction with the agent and the language can also generate
learning that makes the language persist in the portfolio. Suppose the
developer observes signals
\begin{equation}
x_{\ell}=\theta_{ik}+\varepsilon_{\ell},
\qquad
\varepsilon_{\ell}\sim\N(0,\sigma_{\ell}^2),
\qquad
\ell=1,\ldots,L,
\label{eq:signals}
\end{equation}
conditionally independent given $\theta_{ik}$. Let
$q=\sum_{\ell=1}^L1/\sigma_{\ell}^2$ be the total signal precision and
$\bar{x}_q=(\sum_{\ell}x_\ell/\sigma_\ell^2)/q$ the precision-weighted
signal mean. The posterior kernel is proportional to
\[
\exp\left\{
-\frac{1}{2}\pi(\theta-\mu)^2
-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\frac{(x_\ell-\theta)^2}{\sigma_\ell^2}
\right\},
\]
and collecting terms in $\theta$ gives the Bayesian update
\begin{equation}
\pi'_{ik}=\pi_{ik}+q,
\qquad
\mu'_{ik}=
\frac{\pi_{ik}\mu_{ik}+q\bar{x}_q}{\pi_{ik}+q}.
\label{eq:bayes-update}
\end{equation}
Learning raises precision and updates the productivity belief, so an
initially delegated language can remain active in later months. We use
this channel to interpret persistence and cumulative expansion, but not
as the primary proof of immediate diversification: information can
reveal bad matches as well as good ones.

source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
\begin{proposition}[Repository expansion]
\label{prop:repos}
Suppose each repository requires at least one programming language and carries
an entry cost that is weakly decreasing when the developer can activate that
language. If agentic delegation weakly expands the active-language set, then
the expected number of repositories the developer can contribute to weakly
increases. It increases strictly when some repositories require languages in
the delegation activation band.
\end{proposition}

def production_mode_surplusesSpec
    (opportunity skill mean ability capability delegationShare riskAversion precision
      activationCost copilotGain copilotCost delegationCost : ℝ)
    (agentCompetence : ℝ → ℝ) (verificationCost : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (residualVariance : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (hskill : 0 ≤ skill ∧ skill ≤ 1) (hability : 0 ≤ ability)
    (hdelegationShare : 0 < delegationShare ∧ delegationShare ≤ 1)
    (hriskAversion : 0 < riskAversion) (hprecision : 0 < precision) : Prop := soloSurplus opportunity skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost =
      opportunity + skill * mean - riskAversion * skill ^ 2 / (2 * precision) -
        activationCost ∧
    copilotSurplus opportunity skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost
        copilotGain copilotCost =
      soloSurplus opportunity skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost +
        copilotGain * skill - copilotCost ∧
    delegationSurplus opportunity skill mean ability capability delegationShare
        riskAversion precision activationCost delegationCost agentCompetence
        verificationCost residualVariance =
      opportunity + (1 - delegationShare) * skill * mean +
        delegationShare * ability * agentCompetence capability -
        verificationCost ability skill - delegationCost - activationCost -
        riskAversion / 2 *
          (((1 - delegationShare) ^ 2 * skill ^ 2) / precision +
            residualVariance ability skill capability)

    let signalPrecision := totalSignalPrecision signals signalVariance

    signalPrecision = ∑ signal ∈ signals, 1 / signalVariance signal ∧

      posteriorPrecision priorPrecision signalPrecision = priorPrecision + signalPrecision ∧

        (priorPrecision * priorMean + signalPrecision * weightedSignalMean) /
          (priorPrecision + signalPrecision) ∧
      priorPrecision < posteriorPrecision priorPrecision signalPrecision

  ∀ {Repository : Type*} (repositories : Finset Repository)
      (oldCost newCost : Repository → ℝ)
      (opportunityLaw : Repository → MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ),
    (∀ repository, opportunityLaw repository Set.univ = 1) →
    (∀ repository ∈ repositories, newCost repository ≤ oldCost repository) →
    ((∑ repository ∈ repositories,
          (opportunityLaw repository).real (Set.Ici (oldCost repository))) ≤
      (∑ repository ∈ repositories,
          (opportunityLaw repository).real (Set.Ici (newCost repository)))) ∧
    ((∃ repository ∈ repositories,
        0 < (opportunityLaw repository).real
          (Set.Ico (newCost repository) (oldCost repository))) →
      (∑ repository ∈ repositories,
          (opportunityLaw repository).real (Set.Ici (oldCost repository))) <
        ∑ repository ∈ repositories,
          (opportunityLaw repository).real (Set.Ici (newCost repository)))

source_anchor_evidence.quoted_text:
The pre-agent menu is $\mathcal{M}_1=\{S,C\}$; agentic adoption expands it
to $\mathcal{M}_2=\{S,C,D\}$. Under generation $g$ the developer takes the
best available mode, $V^g_{ik,t}=\max_{m\in\mathcal{M}_g}V^m_{ik,t}$, and
language $k$ is \emph{active} when $Z^g_{ik,t}=\1{V^g_{ik,t}\ge0}$, so the
monthly language count is $N^g_{it}=\sum_k Z^g_{ik,t}$.

Because each surplus is affine in the opportunity shock $\omega$, each
mode has an activation threshold. Setting $V^S\ge0$ in Equation
\eqref{eq:solo-surplus}, solo production is viable when
\begin{equation}
\omega\ge
T^S\equiv b-s\mu+\frac{\rho s^2}{2\pi},
\label{eq:solo-threshold}
\end{equation}
and since $V^C=V^S+\gamma s-r_C$, augmentation is viable when
$\omega\ge T^C=T^S-(\gamma s-r_C)$. The developer takes whichever
pre-agent mode clears first, so the effective Generation-1 threshold is
\begin{equation}
T^1=\min\{T^S,T^C\}
=T^S-\max\{0,\gamma s-r_C\},
\label{eq:gen1-threshold}
\end{equation}
and for an unfamiliar language Assumption \ref{ass:foothold} implies
$\gamma s-r_C\le0$, hence $T^1=T^S$: augmentation does not move the
entry margin. Setting $V^D\ge0$ in Equation \eqref{eq:delegate-surplus},
delegation is viable when
\begin{align}
\omega\ge T^D
\equiv{}&
b-(1-\lambda)s\mu-\lambda a z(A)
+\kappa(a,s)+r_D
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(1-\lambda)^2s^2}{\pi}
+\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right],
\label{eq:delegate-threshold}
\end{align}
so the post-agent threshold is $T^2=\min\{T^1,T^D\}\le T^1$.

For an unfamiliar language, the economics reduce to the \emph{agentic
threshold reduction} $B\equiv T^1-T^D=T^S-T^D$. Differencing Equations
\eqref{eq:solo-threshold} and \eqref{eq:delegate-threshold} (algebra in
Appendix \ref{app:proofs}) gives
\begin{equation}
B
=
\lambda\bigl[a z(A)-s\mu\bigr]
-\kappa(a,s)-r_D
+\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(2\lambda-\lambda^2)s^2}{\pi}
-\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right].
\label{eq:agentic-advantage}
\end{equation}
The first term is expected execution substitution: agentic output
replaces a share $\lambda$ of the human's uncertain language-specific
output with agent execution $a z(A)$. The second is the verification and
compute cost of delegating. The third is risk substitution: delegation
shrinks the variance attached to the human match but introduces residual
agent-error risk. If $B>0$, delegation lowers the entry threshold for
the unfamiliar language, and by Assumption \ref{ass:verification} the
reduction is larger for higher-ability developers and more capable
agents.

There are developers $i$, programming languages $k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$, and
months $t$. Developer $i$ has a familiar-language set $\mathcal{K}_i$ and
an unfamiliar set $\mathcal{U}_i$ with $U_i\equiv|\mathcal{U}_i|$; a
specialist is a developer with small $|\mathcal{K}_i|$ and therefore many
unfamiliar candidates. Empirically, ``unfamiliar'' means not observed in
the developer's prior public GitHub contributions; it need not imply
that the developer has no private experience with the language. For each developer--language pair, $s_{ik,t}\in[0,1]$
is language-specific execution skill, and the developer holds Normal
beliefs $\theta_{ik}\sim\N(\mu_{ik,t},1/\pi_{ik,t})$ about her latent
productivity match, with low skill and low precision in unfamiliar
languages. General ability $a_i\ge0$ --- the capacity to specify,
decompose, and verify a task --- is language-invariant. Each language-month
carries an opportunity value $\omega_{ik,t}$ and an activation cost
$b_{ik,t}$. The developer has CARA utility with coefficient $\rho$, so a
payoff with mean $m$ and variance $\sigma^2$ has certainty equivalent
$m-\rho\sigma^2/2$ (Appendix \ref{app:proofs}).

Suppressing $(i,k,t)$ subscripts, the three modes deliver net
certainty-equivalent surpluses
\begin{align}
V^S &= \omega+s\mu-\frac{\rho s^2}{2\pi}-b,
\label{eq:solo-surplus}\\
V^C &= V^S+\gamma s-r_C,
\label{eq:copilot-surplus}\\
V^D &= \omega+(1-\lambda)s\mu+\lambda a z(A)
-\kappa(a,s)-r_D-b
-\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(1-\lambda)^2s^2}{\pi}
+\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right].
\label{eq:delegate-surplus}
\end{align}
Solo production exposes the developer to uncertainty about her own match.
Generation-1 augmentation yields a deterministic gain $\gamma s$
proportional to existing skill, net of interaction cost $r_C$: the
developer benefits most when she can read, adapt, and verify the
suggestion herself. Generation-2 delegation hands a share
$\lambda\in(0,1]$ of execution to an agent with competence $z(A)$,
increasing in capability $A$ and scaled by the developer's general
ability; it carries verification cost $\kappa(a,s)$, compute cost $r_D$,
and residual error variance $\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)$, while shrinking the
variance attached to the human match from $s^2/\pi$ to
$(1-\lambda)^2 s^2/\pi$.

The pre-agent menu is $\mathcal{M}_1=\{S,C\}$; agentic adoption expands it
to $\mathcal{M}_2=\{S,C,D\}$. Under generation $g$ the developer takes the
best available mode, $V^g_{ik,t}=\max_{m\in\mathcal{M}_g}V^m_{ik,t}$, and
language $k$ is \emph{active} when $Z^g_{ik,t}=\1{V^g_{ik,t}\ge0}$, so the
monthly language count is $N^g_{it}=\sum_k Z^g_{ik,t}$.

\begin{assumption}[Comparable unfamiliar-language candidates]
\label{ass:exchangeable}
Conditional on developer characteristics such as general ability, all
unfamiliar languages have the same per-language activation increment
$p_i(a_i,A)\ge0$, and $p_i$ is increasing in $a_i$ whenever Assumption
\ref{ass:verification} makes delegation thresholds fall with ability.
\end{assumption}

dimensions.required_check: Compare every expanded Lean binder domain, result quantifier, and proposition against the literal source statement. Check direction, scope, endpoint, and fixed-versus-uniform quantification; alpha-renaming is not a semantic change. For every formula used as a transformed density, likelihood, kernel, or probability law, check its sign, normalization, and Jacobian factor across the entire declared parameter domain. An algebraic scaling formula is not a probability-law conclusion outside the domain where those facts are proved.

Compare the Lean carrier, finiteness/order/subtype restrictions, and every generic Type/Sort quantifier with the source domain. An arbitrary carrier or a silently strengthened finite carrier needs a source anchor or a checked bridge. When an expanded finite carrier encodes a source cardinal parameter through index arithmetic such as Fin (n + c), state the source parameter, the Lean expression, and a proved translation; local type names and inferred cardinality are not evidence. When a strict conclusion needs distinct, non-endpoint, or interior carrier elements, derive the exact cardinality threshold and witness from the source; a bare source phrase such as 'n candidates' does not supply N >= 3. When the generated surface requests a cardinality-boundary analysis, record the source and Lean cardinal domains, every smallest/endpoint case checked, and either the strictness witness or a semantic reason no such witness is needed. A theorem, wrapper, or carrier name is not that analysis. A local opaque/constant/axiom carrier must expose a checked refinement before it is treated as ordinary model data.

For a finite/ordered probabilistic model, derive support at each endpoint from the source condition actually stated. Strict adjacent-tail comparisons do not by themselves supply a terminal cutoff or positive top/bottom atom; inspect zero mass, degenerate, and boundary cases separately.

Identify the source stochastic process and the Lean joint law separately. Do not replace a source state recurrence, conditioning rule, or time-indexed law with an iid/product construction without a Lean-checked equality, simulation, or refinement from the source primitives. If either side sorts, ranks, relabels, or quotients samples before computing an outcome, prove the corresponding pushforward and outcome-equivariance bridge; matching marginal tables or an informal exchangeability argument is not enough. When the generated surface requests transformed-law analysis, record the source and Lean operations, the full parameter domain including sign/zero endpoints, normalization or pushforward evidence, and outcome-equivariance evidence (or an explicit semantic no-transform/no-relabeling finding). Separately write the source and Lean distribution parameterizations: the exact scale/rate/precision/standard-deviation/variance convention, the parameter mapping formula, and a checked law equality or outcome-preservation bridge. A positive reparameterization or matching declaration name is not a law-equivalence argument. When a standard Measure/Kernel carrier transport is present, identify the source carrier and the Lean carrier, show whether every stage is one joint draw or a source-defined conditional kernel composition, and classify the measure as a source pushforward, source conditioning/restriction, source-defined joint kernel law, generated product/kernel measure, or weighted/tilted measure. A weighted likelihood measure is not a source pushforward without an explicit transport theorem. A rate-free or rate-indexed source claim needs a checked rate-indexed family bridge, not one selected Lean rate. When the elaborated surface contains a ReflTransGen path and a relation-valued state transition, identify the concrete source executor, initial/terminal states, and transition relation; a caller-supplied trace, serialization, or refinement package requires its own checked construction from source primitives.

State exactly whether source and Lean use a pointwise conditional law, an almost-everywhere conditional version, positive-fiber identities, or measurable-event calibration. Expand the event, sigma-algebra/measurability, and joint-law formula; a statement about exact fibers does not silently determine atomless or null fibers. Any switch among these semantics needs a Lean-checked bridge, not a source-looking conditional-probability or calibration name.

For every source or Lean expectation/integral reached through this model, identify the law and integrand and establish the exact definedness convention: measurability or a.e.-measurability, integrability/finite integral, or an explicitly extended-value integral. A displayed E[...] is not a total Real number merely because a predictor or classifier was named; indicator and strategy correctness functions require their own measurability/integrability bridge.

For every conditioning/partition formula reached through this model, compare finite, countable, and arbitrary partition scope; cell measurability, disjointness, and cover on the relevant support; and the value assigned when a cell has zero mass. Expand every ratio/branch used to totalize zero denominators. A finite measurable-cell proof or a positive-mass-only identity does not cover an advertised arbitrary partition without a Lean-checked refinement.

Compare the source rate codomain with the Lean codomain after unfolding the rate definition. A Real-valued formula is not automatically a WithTop/extended-real statement: account for eventual-zero events, infinite rates, zero sample counts, and boundary minimizers.

def production_mode_surplusesSpec
    (opportunity skill mean ability capability delegationShare riskAversion precision
      activationCost copilotGain copilotCost delegationCost : ℝ)
    (agentCompetence : ℝ → ℝ) (verificationCost : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (residualVariance : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (hskill : 0 ≤ skill ∧ skill ≤ 1) (hability : 0 ≤ ability)
    (hdelegationShare : 0 < delegationShare ∧ delegationShare ≤ 1)
    (hriskAversion : 0 < riskAversion) (hprecision : 0 < precision) : Prop := soloSurplus opportunity skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost =
      opportunity + skill * mean - riskAversion * skill ^ 2 / (2 * precision) -
        activationCost ∧
    copilotSurplus opportunity skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost
        copilotGain copilotCost =
      soloSurplus opportunity skill mean riskAversion precision activationCost +
        copilotGain * skill - copilotCost ∧
    delegationSurplus opportunity skill mean ability capability delegationShare
        riskAversion precision activationCost delegationCost agentCompetence
        verificationCost residualVariance =
      opportunity + (1 - delegationShare) * skill * mean +
        delegationShare * ability * agentCompetence capability -
        verificationCost ability skill - delegationCost - activationCost -
        riskAversion / 2 *
          (((1 - delegationShare) ^ 2 * skill ^ 2) / precision +
            residualVariance ability skill capability)

source_claim_atom_contexts.semantic_claim: The source model assigns skill, general ability, opportunity, activation cost, CARA risk aversion, and Normal productivity beliefs, then defines the solo, conversational-assistant, and delegation certainty-equivalent surpluses by Equations (1)-(3).
source_claim_atom_contexts.source_quote:
There are developers $i$, programming languages $k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$, and
months $t$. Developer $i$ has a familiar-language set $\mathcal{K}_i$ and
an unfamiliar set $\mathcal{U}_i$ with $U_i\equiv|\mathcal{U}_i|$; a
specialist is a developer with small $|\mathcal{K}_i|$ and therefore many
unfamiliar candidates. Empirically, ``unfamiliar'' means not observed in
the developer's prior public GitHub contributions; it need not imply
that the developer has no private experience with the language. For each developer--language pair, $s_{ik,t}\in[0,1]$
is language-specific execution skill, and the developer holds Normal
beliefs $\theta_{ik}\sim\N(\mu_{ik,t},1/\pi_{ik,t})$ about her latent
productivity match, with low skill and low precision in unfamiliar
languages. General ability $a_i\ge0$ --- the capacity to specify,
decompose, and verify a task --- is language-invariant. Each language-month
carries an opportunity value $\omega_{ik,t}$ and an activation cost
$b_{ik,t}$. The developer has CARA utility with coefficient $\rho$, so a
payoff with mean $m$ and variance $\sigma^2$ has certainty equivalent
$m-\rho\sigma^2/2$ (Appendix \ref{app:proofs}).

Suppressing $(i,k,t)$ subscripts, the three modes deliver net
certainty-equivalent surpluses
\begin{align}
V^S &= \omega+s\mu-\frac{\rho s^2}{2\pi}-b,
\label{eq:solo-surplus}\\
V^C &= V^S+\gamma s-r_C,
\label{eq:copilot-surplus}\\
V^D &= \omega+(1-\lambda)s\mu+\lambda a z(A)
-\kappa(a,s)-r_D-b
-\frac{\rho}{2}
\left[
\frac{(1-\lambda)^2s^2}{\pi}
+\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)
\right].
\label{eq:delegate-surplus}
\end{align}
Solo production exposes the developer to uncertainty about her own match.
Generation-1 augmentation yields a deterministic gain $\gamma s$
proportional to existing skill, net of interaction cost $r_C$: the
developer benefits most when she can read, adapt, and verify the
suggestion herself. Generation-2 delegation hands a share
$\lambda\in(0,1]$ of execution to an agent with competence $z(A)$,
increasing in capability $A$ and scaled by the developer's general
ability; it carries verification cost $\kappa(a,s)$, compute cost $r_D$,
and residual error variance $\sigma_D^2(a,s,A)$, while shrinking the
variance attached to the human match from $s^2/\pi$ to
$(1-\lambda)^2 s^2/\pi$.
